review.plain: Knowingly presenting a false or fraudulent claim or proof of loss to a motor vehicle, theft or comprehensive insurer, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison plus restitution.
acts: knowingly presents to it, or aids or abets in or procures the presentation to it of, any notice, statement, or proof of loss

crimes.act: Presents to an insurer, or aids or abets in or procures the presentation to it of, any notice, statement, or proof of loss, in connection with or in support of any application for or claim under any motor vehicle, theft or comprehensive insurance policy
ways: aids or abets in the presentation of
conditions: The notice, statement or proof of loss contains a false or fraudulent statement or representation of a fact or thing material to the application or claim
It is presented whether or not it is under oath or is required or authorized by law or the terms of the policy

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or 6 months to 2½ years in a house of correction, or a fine of $1,000 to $10,000, or both a fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing that the notice, statement or proof of loss contains a false or fraudulent statement or representation of a material fact or thing
intent: With intent to injure, defraud or deceive the insurer
consequences: After conviction, the court conducts an evidentiary hearing on the damages or financial loss

Restitution to the insurer for financial loss must be ordered, in addition to any other punishment and not in lieu of incarceration or fine; not ordered to an aggrieved party without that party's consent
Court considers the defendant's present and future ability to pay when setting a fine; whenever possible the fine equals twice the damages or financial loss

A licensed motor vehicle damage appraiser or registered motor vehicle repair shop who violates this section by fraudulently inflating an appraisal or repair charges also faces revocation of the license or registration for up to two years
Default on restitution without good faith effort leads to contempt; with good faith effort the court may modify but not completely remit payment

review.plain: Knowingly acting as a runner, or using, hiring or directing one, to defraud an insured or insurance carrier is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: acts as a runner or uses, solicits, directs, hires or employs another to act as a runner

crimes.act: Acts as a runner or uses, solicits, directs, hires or employs another to act as a runner
ways: uses another to act as a runner
solicits another to act as a runner
directs another to act as a runner
hires another to act as a runner
employs another to act as a runner
exceptions: "Runner" does not include a person who procures or attempts to procure clients, patients or customers for a provider through public media or a person who refers clients, patients or customers to a provider as otherwise authorized by law

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or 6 months to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of $1,000 to $4,000

intent: For the purpose of defrauding an insured or an insurance carrier
terms: "Provider": an attorney, a health care professional licensed pursuant to chapter 112, an owner or operator of a health care practice or facility, any person who creates the impression that he or his practice or facility can provide legal or health care services, or any person employed or acting on behalf of any of them

"Public media": telephone directories, professional directories, newspapers and other periodicals, radio and television, billboards and mailed or electronically transmitted written communications that do not involve in-person contact with a specific prospective client, patient or customer

"Runner": a person who, for a pecuniary benefit, procures or attempts to procure a client, patient or customer at the direction of, request of, or in cooperation with a provider whose purpose is to seek to fraudulently obtain benefits under a contract of insurance or fraudulently assert a claim against an insured or an insurance carrier for providing services to the client, patient or customer

review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously killing, maiming or disfiguring another person's animal, or poisoning it, is punishable by up to 7 years in state prison, and up to 10 years for a repeat offense.
acts: kills, maims or disfigures any horse, cattle or other animal of another person
administers or exposes poison with intent that it shall be taken or swallowed by any such animal

crimes.act: Kills, maims or disfigures any horse, cattle or other animal of another person

penalties.penalty: Up to 7 years in state prison, or up to 2 1/2 years in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $5,000, or both fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: it is a second or subsequent offense
penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $10,000, or both

crimes.act: Administers or exposes poison with intent that it shall be taken or swallowed by any such animal
intent: With intent that the poison be taken or swallowed by any such animal

penalties.penalty: Up to 7 years in state prison, or up to 2 1/2 years in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $5,000, or both fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: it is a second or subsequent offense
penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $10,000, or both

review.plain: Wilfully cutting, taking or destroying timber, plants, stone, soil or similar things on another's land without the owner's license is punishable by up to six months in jail or a $500 fine.
acts: wilfully cuts down or destroys timber or wood standing or growing on the land of another
carries away any kind of timber or wood cut down or lying on such land
digs up or carries away stone, ore, gravel, clay, sand, turf or mould from such land
cuts down or carries away sedge, grass, hay or any kind of corn, standing, growing or being on such land
roots, nuts, berries, grapes or fruit of any kind or any plant there being
cuts or takes therefrom any ferns, flowers or shrubs
carries away from a wharf or landing place any goods in which he has no interest or property

penalties.penalty: Up to six months imprisonment or a fine of up to five hundred dollars

penalties.if: the offence is committed on Sunday, or in disguise, or secretly in the night time
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment of not less than five days and a fine of not less than five dollars (within the penalty above)

crimes.act: Cuts down or destroys timber or wood standing or growing on the land of another
Carries away any kind of timber or wood cut down or lying on such land
Digs up or carries away stone, ore, gravel, clay, sand, turf or mould from such land
Digs up or carries away roots, nuts, berries, grapes or fruit of any kind or any plant there being
Cuts down or carries away sedge, grass, hay or any kind of corn, standing, growing or being on such land
Cuts or takes ferns, flowers or shrubs from such land
Carries away from a wharf or landing place any goods in which he has no interest or property
conditions: The person has no interest or property in the goods

review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously (or wantonly) breaking glass in another's building, damaging fences or gates, or severing produce from another's land is punishable by up to six months or a $500 fine.
acts: breaks glass in a building which is not his own
breaks down, injures, mars or defaces a fence belonging to or enclosing land which is not his own
throws down or opens a gate, bars or fence, and leaves the same down or open
severs from the freehold of another any produce thereof or anything attached thereto

penalties.penalty: Up to six months imprisonment or a fine of up to five hundred dollars

crimes.act: Breaks glass in a building which is not his own
Breaks down, injures, mars or defaces a fence belonging to or enclosing land which is not his own
Throws down or opens a gate, bars or fence, and leaves the same down or open
Severs from the freehold of another any produce thereof or anything attached thereto

review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously entering an orchard, nursery, garden or cranberry meadow and taking or destroying plants or fruit without consent is punishable by up to six months or a $500 fine.
acts: enters an orchard, nursery, garden or cranberry meadow, and takes away, mutilates or destroys a tree, shrub or vine, or steals, takes and carries away any fruit or flower

crimes.act: Enters an orchard, nursery, garden or cranberry meadow, and takes away, mutilates or destroys a tree, shrub or vine, or steals, takes and carries away any fruit or flower
ways: takes away a tree, shrub or vine
mutilates a tree, shrub or vine
destroys a tree, shrub or vine
steals, takes and carries away any fruit or flower
conditions: Without the consent of the owner

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to five hundred dollars or imprisonment for up to six months

review.plain: Pulling up, digging up or injuring wild azalea, wild orchid or cardinal flower plants in public places or on another's land without written authority, or buying or selling them, is punishable by a fine of up to $5.
acts: pull up or dig up the plant of a wild azalea, wild orchid or cardinal flower (lobelia cardinalis), or any part thereof
injure any such plant or any part thereof
buy or sell, or offer or expose for sale, any such flower, or the whole or any part of the plant thereof

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to five dollars

crimes.act: Pulls up or digs up the plant of a wild azalea, wild orchid or cardinal flower (lobelia cardinalis), or any part thereof, or injures any such plant or any part thereof
conditions: Within the limits of any state highway or any other public way or place, or upon the land of another person without written authority from him
exceptions: Injury reasonably necessary in procuring the flower from the plant

crimes.act: Buys or sells, or offers or exposes for sale, any such flower, or the whole or any part of the plant thereof
knowledge: Knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, that in procuring such flower or plant the foregoing provisions have been violated

review.plain: Wilfully and intentionally entering another's orchard, garden or improved land without right, intending to cut, take or destroy plants or produce, is punishable by up to six months or a $500 fine.
acts: enters upon the orchard, garden or other improved land of another

penalties.penalty: Up to six months imprisonment or a fine of up to five hundred dollars

penalties.if: the offence is committed on Sunday, or in disguise, or secretly in the night time
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment of not less than five days and a fine of not less than five dollars (within the penalty above)

crimes.act: Enters upon the orchard, garden or other improved land of another
conditions: Without right
intent: With intent to cut, take, carry away, destroy or injure the trees, grain, grass, hay, fruit or vegetables there growing or being

review.plain: Wilfully letting sheep, goats, cattle, horses, swine or fowl in your charge stay on or cross another's improved land after written or posted notice is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: suffers or permits them to enter or remain on or pass over any orchard, garden, mowing land or other improved or enclosed land of another

crimes.act: Suffers or permits sheep, goats, cattle, horses, swine or fowl to enter or remain on or pass over any orchard, garden, mowing land or other improved or enclosed land of another
conditions: After being forbidden so to do in writing or by notice posted thereon by the owner or occupant, or by the authorized agent of such owner or occupant

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to ten dollars

crimes.who: A person having the charge or custody of sheep, goats, cattle, horses, swine or fowl

review.plain: Knowingly bringing a regulated pest into the commonwealth, moving it between towns, or evading a quarantine regulation is punishable by a fine of up to $200, up to two months in jail, or both.
acts: brings into the commonwealth, or transports from one town to another therein, any pest referred to in section eleven or twenty-five of chapter one hundred and thirty-two, or the eggs, nests, larvae or pupae thereof
evades the requirements of a quarantine regulation duly established under any provision of said chapter one hundred and thirty-two

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $200, or imprisonment for up to two months, or both

crimes.act: Brings into the commonwealth, or transports from one town to another therein, any pest referred to in section eleven or twenty-five of chapter one hundred and thirty-two, or the eggs, nests, larvae or pupae thereof
ways: transports from one town to another
exceptions: When engaged in research work for the commonwealth or for the United States department of agriculture, and for the purpose of suppressing such pests

crimes.act: Evades the requirements of a quarantine regulation duly established under any provision of said chapter one hundred and thirty-two

review.plain: Entering or remaining on another's building or land, or in a school bus, after being forbidden, or violating a related court order, is punishable by a fine of up to $100 or up to 30 days in jail.
acts: enters or remains in or upon the dwelling house, buildings, boats or improved or enclosed land, wharf, or pier of another
enters or remains in a school bus, as defined in section 1 of chapter 90

crimes.act: Enters or remains in or upon the dwelling house, buildings, boats or improved or enclosed land, wharf, or pier of another, or enters or remains in a school bus
conditions: Without right

After having been forbidden so to do by the person who has lawful control of the premises, whether directly or by notice posted thereon, or in violation of a court order pursuant to section thirty-four B of chapter two hundred and eight or section three or four of chapter two hundred and nine A
exceptions: This section does not apply to tenants or occupants of residential premises who, having rightfully entered at the commencement of the tenancy or occupancy, remain after the tenancy or occupancy has been or is alleged to have been terminated

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to one hundred dollars or imprisonment for up to thirty days or both

terms: Proof that a court has given notice of such a court order to the alleged offender is prima facie evidence that the notice requirement has been met
consequences: A person found committing the trespass may be arrested by a sheriff, deputy sheriff, constable or police officer and kept in custody not more than twenty-four hours, Sunday excepted, until a complaint can be made

review.plain: Provides that, in a prosecution for trespass by parking a motor vehicle on a private way or enclosed land, proof that the defendant was the registered owner is prima facie evidence the defendant parked it.
Provides that an abutting landowner who enters adjoining land to maintain or repair a building is not guilty of trespass or civilly liable if notice, bond and other conditions are met.
Provides that a registered land surveyor entering adjoining lands after reasonable notice to make surveys for a private person is not trespassing, but remains liable for damage caused.
Removing a vehicle from a private way or property without notifying police or the owner's consent, or purporting to authorize such removal without complying, is punishable by a fine of up to $100.
acts: removes a vehicle from a private way or from improved or enclosed property as aforesaid
purports to authorize the removal of a vehicle from a way or property as aforesaid without having fully complied with the provision of this section

crimes.act: Removes a motor vehicle which is parked or standing on a private way or upon improved or enclosed property without notifying the chief of police or his designee, or the police commissioner or his designee, or without obtaining the consent of the owner
ways: removes a vehicle without notifying the police
removes a vehicle without the owner's consent
conditions: The vehicle is removed from a private way or from improved or enclosed property

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to one hundred dollars

consequences: In addition to any other penalty of law
The employer of the person, if any, is also punished by a fine of up to one hundred dollars
The registered owner of an illegally parked vehicle is liable for removal and storage charges, subject to the limits in this section, if the vehicle was removed after compliance with this section
A vehicle removed or held without full compliance must be released to its owner without charges for removal or storage

crimes.act: Purports to authorize the removal of a vehicle from a way or property as aforesaid without having fully complied with the provision of this section

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to one hundred dollars

review.plain: Knowingly obstructing entry to or departure from a medical facility, or entering or remaining so as to impede services, after notice is punishable by up to six months in jail, and up to 2½ years for repeat violations.
acts: knowingly obstructs entry to or departure from any medical facility
enters or remains in any medical facility so as to impede the provision of medical services

terms: "Medical facility": any medical office, medical clinic, medical laboratory, or hospital

"Notice": (i) receipt of or awareness of the contents of a court order prohibiting blocking of a medical facility; (ii) oral request by an authorized representative of a medical facility, or law enforcement official to refrain from obstructing access to a medical facility; or (iii) written posted notice outside the entrance to a medical facility to refrain from obstructing access to a medical facility

penalties.penalty: First offense: A fine of up to one thousand dollars or up to six months in jail or a house of correction or both
A fine of $500 to $5,000 or up to two and one-half years in jail or a house of correction or both

consequences: These penalties are in addition to any penalties imposed for violation of a court order
The person may be arrested by a sheriff, deputy sheriff, constable, or police officer
The medical facility may bring a civil action for injunctive and other equitable relief, including compensatory and exemplary damages, costs and reasonable attorney's fees

crimes.act: Obstructs entry to or departure from any medical facility
conditions: After notice to refrain from such obstruction or interference
defenses: Peaceful picketing which does not obstruct entry or departure is not interfered with by this section

crimes.act: Enters or remains in any medical facility so as to impede the provision of medical services
conditions: After notice to refrain from such obstruction or interference
defenses: Peaceful picketing which does not obstruct entry or departure is not interfered with by this section

review.plain: Defying a police withdrawal order at a reproductive health care facility, or injuring, intimidating, impeding or interfering with people or vehicles there, is punishable by fines or jail, up to 5 years in state prison for some repeat offenses.
acts: fails to comply with a withdrawal order pursuant to subsection (b)
intentionally injures or intimidates or attempts to injure or intimidate a person who attempts to access or depart from a reproductive health care facility
impedes a person's access to or departure from a reproductive health care facility
impedes or attempts to impede a person or a vehicle attempting to access or depart from a reproductive health care facility
interferes with the operation of a vehicle that attempts to enter, exit or park at a reproductive health care facility

terms: "Driveway": an entry from a public street to a public or private parking area used by a reproductive health care facility

"Entrance": a door to a reproductive health care facility that directly abuts the public sidewalk; if the door does not directly abut the public sidewalk, the point at which the public sidewalk intersects with a pathway leading to the door
"Impede": to obstruct, block, detain or render passage impossible, unsafe or unreasonably difficult

"Reproductive health care facility": a place, other than within or upon the grounds of a hospital, where abortions are offered or performed including, but not limited to, the building, grounds and driveway of the facility and a parking lot in which the facility has an ownership or leasehold interest
consequences: A person who fails to comply with a withdrawal order or violates subsection (c), (d), (e), (f) or (g) may be arrested without a warrant by a law enforcement official

An aggrieved person or entity or the attorney general may bring a civil action for injunctive relief, compensatory and punitive damages, costs, attorneys' fees and expert witness fees; the attorney general may also seek civil penalties
A violation of an injunction entered in such an action is a criminal offense under section 11J of chapter 12

crimes.act: Fails to comply with a withdrawal order pursuant to subsection (b)
conditions: A law enforcement official issued a written withdrawal order to the person under subsection (b)

penalties.penalty: First offense: A fine of up to $500 or up to 3 months in a jail or house of correction or both
A fine of $500 to $5,000 or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction or both

crimes.act: Injures or intimidates or attempts to injure or intimidate a person who attempts to access or depart from a reproductive health care facility, by force, physical act or threat of force

penalties.penalty: First offense: A fine of up to $2,000 or up to 1 year in a jail or house of correction or both
A fine of $10,000 to $50,000, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction or up to 5 years in a state prison, or both a fine and imprisonment

terms: "Intimidate": to place a person in reasonable apprehension of bodily harm to that person or another

crimes.act: Impedes a person's access to or departure from a reproductive health care facility

penalties.penalty: First offense: A fine of up to $1,000 or up to 6 months in a jail or house of correction or both
A fine of $5,000 to $25,000, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction or up to 5 years in the state prison, or both a fine and imprisonment

intent: With the intent to interfere with that person's ability to provide, support the provision of or obtain services at the reproductive health care facility

crimes.act: Impedes or attempts to impede a person or a vehicle attempting to access or depart from a reproductive health care facility

penalties.penalty: First offense: A fine of up to $500 or up to 3 months in a jail or house of correction or both
A fine of $1,000 to $5,000 or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction or both

crimes.act: Interferes with the operation of a vehicle that attempts to enter, exit or park at a reproductive health care facility

penalties.penalty: First offense: A fine of up to $500 or up to 3 months in a jail or house of correction or both
A fine of $1,000 to $5,000 or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction or both

review.plain: Knowingly accessing a computer system without authorization, or staying in after learning access is unauthorized, is punishable by up to 30 days in a house of correction or a fine of up to $1,000.
acts: accesses a computer system by any means
fails to terminate such access

crimes.act: Accesses a computer system by any means, or after gaining access to a computer system by any means fails to terminate such access
ways: fails to terminate access after gaining it
conditions: Without authorization
For failure to terminate, the person knows that the access is not authorized

penalties.penalty: Up to thirty days in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $1,000, or both

terms: The requirement of a password or other authentication to gain access constitutes notice that access is limited to authorized users

review.plain: Entering another's land without right with firearms intending to fire them, and staying after being asked to leave, is punishable by a fine of up to $200, up to two months in jail, or both.
acts: enters upon the land of another with firearms

crimes.act: Enters upon the land of another with firearms and, having been requested by the owner or occupant of such land or by his agent to leave such land, remains thereon
conditions: Without right
Having been requested by the owner or occupant or his agent to leave, the person remains

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to two hundred dollars or imprisonment for up to two months, or both

intent: With intent to fire or discharge the firearms thereon

review.plain: Entering another's private land without right with a motor-powered vehicle, machine or device is punishable by a fine of up to $500.
acts: enters upon the private land of another, whether or not such land be posted against trespass

crimes.act: Enters upon the private land of another and in so entering makes use of or has in his immediate possession or control any vehicle, machine, or device which includes an internal combustion engine or other source of mechanical power
conditions: Without right
Whether or not the land is posted against trespass
exceptions: Entry at the junction of a public way with a paved private roadway, unless the roadway is distinguished from the public way by a sign, gatepost, or the display of a street number or the name of the occupant, or by the improvement of adjacent land, the type of construction of the roadway, or other distinguishing feature, or unless the entry has been forbidden by the person having lawful control
Operation of power boats on waterways not otherwise restricted

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500

review.plain: Wilfully tearing down, removing or defacing a posted no-trespassing notice is punishable by a fine of up to $25.
acts: tears down, removes or defaces any notice posted on land, or other property described in section one hundred and twenty, by the owner, lessee or custodian thereof, warning persons not to trespass thereon

crimes.act: Tears down, removes or defaces any notice posted on land, or other property described in section one hundred and twenty, by the owner, lessee or custodian thereof, warning persons not to trespass thereon

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to twenty-five dollars

review.plain: Willfully trespassing on state land or on listed public institution grounds, or staying after notice to leave, is punishable by a fine of up to $50 or up to three months in jail.
acts: trespasses upon land or premises belonging to the commonwealth
remains thereon

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to fifty dollars or imprisonment for up to three months

crimes.act: Trespasses upon land or premises belonging to the commonwealth, or to any authority established by the general court for purposes incidental to higher education, appurtenant to a public institution of higher education, any correctional institution of the commonwealth, Tewksbury hospital, a state-operated veterans' home, any public institution for the care of mentally ill and developmentally disabled persons, any Massachusetts training school or state charitable institution, or upon land or premises belonging to any county and appurtenant to a jail, house of correction or courthouse
Remains on said land after notice from an officer of any of said institutions to leave
conditions: Notice to leave was given by an officer of one of the institutions

review.plain: Willfully trespassing on public water sources or supply facilities after being forbidden is fined $250 to $1,000; doing so intending to pollute carries up to 5 years in state prison, and up to 10 years for repeats.
acts: trespasses upon any public source of water or public water supply facilities or land
commits any offense described in subsection (a)

consequences: A law enforcement officer may arrest without a warrant any person the officer has probable cause to believe has violated this section

crimes.act: Trespasses upon any public source of water or public water supply facilities or land
conditions: After having been forbidden to do so by a person who has lawful control of the water, facilities or land, or an agent of such a person, whether directly or by notice posted on such water supply facility or land

penalties.penalty: A fine of $250 to $1,000

consequences: Restitution for costs of water quality analysis and subsequent investigation may be ordered by a court after a hearing

crimes.act: Commits any offense described in subsection (a)

penalties.penalty: A fine of $1,000 to $5,000, or up to 2 years in the house of correction or up to 5 years in state prison, or both a fine and imprisonment
A fine of $1,000 to $10,000, or 5 to 10 years in state prison, or both a fine and imprisonment

intent: With the intent to corrupt, pollute or defile such public source of water
consequences: Restitution for costs of water quality analysis and subsequent investigation may be ordered by a court after a hearing

review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously (or wantonly and without cause) tearing down or defacing a lawfully posted town meeting warrant, juror list or notice is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: tears down, removes or defaces a warrant for a town meeting, list of jurors or other notice or paper which has been posted in compliance with law

crimes.act: Tears down, removes or defaces a warrant for a town meeting, list of jurors or other notice or paper which has been posted in compliance with law

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to ten dollars

intent: Wilfully and maliciously, or wantonly and without cause

review.plain: Wilfully and maliciously removing, destroying or mutilating a posted show bill or advertisement for a licensed exhibition before it takes place is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: removes, destroys or mutilates a show bill, placard, program or other advertisement posted upon a wall, fence, billboard or structure not lawfully under his control

crimes.act: Removes, destroys or mutilates a show bill, placard, program or other advertisement posted upon a wall, fence, billboard or structure not lawfully under his control
conditions: The advertisement is for an exhibition, show or amusement licensed under section one hundred and eighty-one of chapter one hundred and forty
The exhibition, show or amusement has not yet taken place

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to ten dollars

review.plain: Painting or affixing unauthorized words, ads or notices on public or another's property without written consent is punishable by a fine of $10 to $100, plus forfeiture of removal costs.
acts: paints, or puts upon, or in any manner affixes to, any fence, structure, pole, rock or other object which is public property or the property of another

crimes.act: Paints, or puts upon, or in any manner affixes to, any fence, structure, pole, rock or other object which is public property or the property of another, any words, device, trade mark, advertisement or notice which is not required by law to be posted thereon
conditions: Without first obtaining the written consent of the municipal or public officer in charge thereof or the owner or tenant of the property
The words, device, trade mark, advertisement or notice is not required by law to be posted

penalties.penalty: A fine of $10 to $100, plus forfeiture of the cost of removal

consequences: Punished upon complaint of the municipal or public officer, or of the owner or tenant
Forfeits to the public or private owner or the tenant the cost of removing or obliterating the defacement, recovered in an action of tort
Any such item placed within the limits of a highway in violation is a public nuisance and may be removed or obliterated and abated by any person

review.plain: Intentionally, willfully and maliciously (or wantonly) defacing or destroying another's property is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison or 2 years in a house of correction, a fine, and paying for cleanup.
acts: paints, marks, scratches, etches or otherwise marks, injures, mars, defaces or destroys the real or personal property of another

crimes.act: Paints, marks, scratches, etches or otherwise marks, injures, mars, defaces or destroys the real or personal property of another

penalties.penalty: Up to 3 years in a state prison, or up to 2 years in a house of correction, or a fine of up to $1,500 or up to three times the value of the property, whichever is greater, or both imprisonment and fine

penalties.if: the property is a war or veterans' memorial, monument or gravestone
penalties.penalty: The fine is doubled and not less than 500 hours of court-approved community service is ordered

intent: Intentionally, willfully and maliciously or wantonly
consequences: Must pay for the removal or obliteration of the painting, marking, scratching or etching, or remove or obliterate it
Court conducts an evidentiary hearing after conviction on the value of the property or the cost of removal when a fine is based on value or removal cost is assessed
If the property is a war or veterans' memorial, monument or gravestone, the fine is doubled and the person must perform not less than 500 hours of court-approved community service
A police officer may arrest without a warrant with probable cause

review.plain: Tagging by spraying paint or placing a sticker on property, alone or with a group, with intent to deface or damage it, is punishable by up to 2 years in a house of correction, a fine, and cleanup costs.
acts: sprays or applies paint or places a sticker upon a building, wall, fence, sign, tablet, gravestone, monument or other object or thing on a public way or adjoined to it, or in public view, or on private property

crimes.act: Sprays or applies paint or places a sticker upon a building, wall, fence, sign, tablet, gravestone, monument or other object or thing on a public way or adjoined to it, or in public view, or on private property
conditions: Done either as an individual or in a group, joining together with said group

penalties.penalty: Up to 2 years in a house of correction, or a fine of not less than $1,500 or up to three times the value of the damage, whichever is greater, or both fine and imprisonment

intent: With the intent to deface, mar, damage, mark or destroy such property
consequences: Must pay for the removal or obliteration of the tagging, or obliterate it
Court conducts an evidentiary hearing after conviction on the value of the property or the cost of removal
A police officer may arrest without a warrant with probable cause

review.plain: Willfully and maliciously destroying or injuring another's personal property, dwelling or building in a way not described elsewhere in this chapter is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison; wanton damage by up to 2½ years.
acts: destroys or injures the personal property, dwelling house or building of another in any manner or by any means not particularly described or mentioned in this chapter

crimes.act: Destroys or injures the personal property, dwelling house or building of another in any manner or by any means not particularly described or mentioned in this chapter

penalties.penalty: If willful and malicious: up to 10 years in state prison, or a fine of $3,000 or 3 times the value of the damage, whichever is greater, and imprisonment in jail for up to 2½ years

penalties.if: the destruction or injury is wanton
penalties.penalty: A fine of $1,000 or 3 times the value of the damage, whichever is greater, or imprisonment for up to 2½ years

penalties.if: the value of the damage is not alleged to exceed $1,200
penalties.penalty: A fine of 3 times the value of the damage or imprisonment for up to 2½ years

terms: "Personal property": also includes electronically processed or stored data, either tangible or intangible, and data while in transit
consequences: Where a fine is levied based on value of damage, the court conducts an evidentiary hearing after conviction to ascertain the value of the damage
intent: Willfully and maliciously (or wantonly, for the lower penalty)

review.plain: Willfully (or wantonly) destroying or defacing a church, burial place, school or community center, or threatening to destroy a place of worship, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison for damage over $5,000.
acts: destroys, defaces, mars, or injures a church, synagogue or other building, structure or place used for the purpose of burial or memorializing the dead
threatens to burn, deface, mar, injure, or in any way destroy a church, synagogue or other building, structure, or place of worship

crimes.act: Destroys, defaces, mars, or injures a church, synagogue or other building, structure or place used for the purpose of burial or memorializing the dead, or a school, educational facility or community center or the grounds adjacent to and owned or leased by any of the foregoing or any personal property contained in any of the foregoing

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $2,000 or up to three times the value of the property, whichever is greater, or imprisonment in a house of correction for up to two and one-half years, or both

penalties.if: the damage to or loss of the property exceeds $5,000
penalties.penalty: A fine of up to three times the value of the property or imprisonment in a state prison for up to five years, or both

intent: Willfully, intentionally and without right, or wantonly and without cause

crimes.act: Threatens to burn, deface, mar, injure, or in any way destroy a church, synagogue or other building, structure, or place of worship

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $1,500, or imprisonment in a jail or house of correction for up to one year, or both
